name: apply-routing-structures
prompt: fixture_apply_routing_structures.py is our 2.4 GHz board. The antenna feed now goes from the U.FL through a via at x = -9 mm and on to the series inductor, and it has a timing constraint. Run the feed as the substrate's CPWG_50, except the short segment from the connector pad to the via, which should use NECK_50. The build currently complains about a missing routing structure; make that go away.
notes: The fixtures import jitxexamples parts from py-components origin/main 9c398d3 (the installed package in the eval venv); the build uses the lc-eval parts chain, the example catalogue then ideal parts, so no parts database is needed. The fixture module is fixture_apply_routing_structures.py, Design ApplyRoutingStructuresDesign. Measured on jitx 4.6: design_constraint(tag).routing_structure(rs, ref_net=GND) on a net tag applies the structure to a code route and clears the Missing routing structure issue; a priority-1 rule on a tag on the escape Route object gives that segment its own structure; a rule on (net tag) & IsTrace hits every segment; a rule silently overrides a .structure(...) on the same net with no issue. A RoutingStructure built at module level is an Instantiable a rule cannot apply (measured on jitx 4.6); this suite's own solution applies the substrate's own LcStandard4.CPWG_50 and LcStandard4.NECK_50, referenced inside the circuit's __init__, and that worked. Measured on the bare fixture (this suite's own run, 2026-11-03): both segments 0.1, Missing routing structure on both paths. This suite's own solution: escape 0.12 with the pour 0.1301 away, main 0.3 with 0.21, timing satisfied and no missing structure. A runner that applies the structures with both a rule and .structure(...) is judged on whether it says which one wins. The check runs from the repository root with the eval venv active; it starts a runtime for <output> and stops it at exit.
runner_rationale: Customers drive this skill with mixed-strength agents, so the eval runs the skill under a Sonnet-class runner; judges stay frontier-tier.
runner_artifacts: The input files are the starting design. Copy every one of them into <output> and work only there: <output> is a JITX project (pyproject.toml) whose modules import each other by file name. Add tags and design rules, applying the substrate's routing structures where the task needs one (a fenced copy of one is fine if its width and clearance are unchanged), in the fixture module, fixture_apply_routing_structures.py, or in a module it imports, and keep its Design class name. Do not add, move or remove parts, nets, routes, vias or pours, and do not set Route.Config on a route; assigning a tag to an existing object is fine. Build the design and read the result back to show the rules applied. Write a completion summary to <output>/COMPLETION.md: each rule with the source of its numbers, what you checked after the build and what it showed, and anything left open. Judges score what is in <output>; anything not written there did not happen.
expected_output: A tag on the RF feed net with a routing_structure rule for CPWG_50, a tag on the feed_escape Route object with a higher-priority routing_structure rule for NECK_50, both with ref_net GND, and COMPLETION.md with each segment's measured width and pour gap and the issue report showing no missing routing structure.

assertions.text: the escape segment is realized at NECK_50's 0.12 mm with the pour 0.12 mm away, the main segment at CPWG_50's 0.30 mm with the pour 0.20 mm away, and the issue report has no missing routing structure
the neck structure is scoped to the escape segment by a tag on that Route object at a higher priority, not by a condition that also catches the main segment
if the runner sets a structure both by rule and by .structure(...), it says the rule wins without an issue; otherwise it uses one mechanism and says which
COMPLETION.md reports widths per segment and the issue report read from the built design, not build success alone
COMPLETION.md gives, for each rule, the electrical need it holds: what goes wrong on this board without it, in a sentence.
